Check family ids against the family trees the parents form

Source: R/familyCheck.R
familyCheck.Rd

Compares the family id each animal is given with the family trees its parent links form. Two animals are in the same tree when a chain of parent-offspring links joins them. A link counts only when the parent has a row (an id in id), so a parent id with no row, such as "0" or "", links no one, as in kinship2. An animal linked to no other is related to no one.

Usage

familyCheck(famid, id, sire, dam, newfam)

Arguments

famid

a vector of family ids, one per animal. NA is not allowed.

id

a vector of unique animal ids. NA is not allowed.

sire

a vector with each animal's sire, NA if unknown.

dam

a vector with each animal's dam, NA if unknown.

newfam

optional: a family-tree number per animal, 0 for an animal related to no one, as kinship2::makefamid() returns. When given it is used as it is, instead of computing the trees.

Value

A data frame with one row per family id, sorted (character ids in byte order, numbers by value), and the columns famid (the family id, of the type given; a factor's as character), n, unrelated, split and join (integers). When any join is above 0, the data frame has an attribute "join": an integer matrix with a row per joined family id and a column per family tree their animals belong to, named by tree number, each entry the number of that family's animals in that tree. Trees are numbered 1, 2, ... in the order of their first animal, as kinship2::makefamid() numbers them.

Details

For each family id, familyCheck() counts its animals (n), those related to no one (unrelated), the trees its other animals fall in (split: 1 is what a family should be; 0 means none of its animals is related to another; 2 or more means it is two or more trees with no link between them), and the other family ids sharing those trees (join: 0 is what a family should be). join counts another family id once for each tree the two share, as kinship2::familycheck() does.

It is kinship2's familycheck() for pedigree vectors whose unknown parents are NA. On every case its tests compare with kinship2 (the fixture pedigrees with family ids given wrongly, and random families), it gives kinship2's counts and join table. It differs where kinship2 stops with an error: when every join lies within one family tree, and for empty input, where it returns zero rows. It sorts character family ids in byte order, where kinship2 follows the locale; keeps the family ids' type and returns integer counts; names the join table's columns by tree number; and stops on a repeated id, which kinship2 accepts. An animal that is its own ancestor does not stop it (kinship2 stops on some such pedigrees).

References

Sinnwell JP, Therneau TM, Schaid DJ (2014). "The kinship2 R Package for Pedigree Data." Human Heredity, 78(2), 91-93.

See also

findPedigreeNumber

Examples

## A and B are the parents of C, and D and E of F; G is related to no one.
## Family "a" is given to A and B, but C, their child, is given "x".
id <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G")
sire <- c(NA, NA, "A", NA, NA, "D", NA)
dam <- c(NA, NA, "B", NA, NA, "E", NA)
famid <- c("a", "a", "x", "b", "b", "b", "b")
result <- familyCheck(famid, id, sire, dam)
result
#>   famid n unrelated split join
#> 1     a 2         0     1    1
#> 2     b 4         1     1    0
#> 3     x 1         0     1    1
attr(result, "join")
#>   1
#> a 2
#> x 1
